segments.title: 第155章 我好,你壞
segments.content:
"Dear teachers and beloved classmates, good morning. I am Li Luo from Class 8 of the first year."

"It is my great honor to stand under the national flag today and share my learning experience with all of you."

After dishing out three minutes of motivational fluff on the national flag platform, Li Luo finished his speech, walked off the stage, and went around to the rest area beside it, finally letting out a sigh of relief.

Ying Chanxi was standing to his right and secretly leaned in to whisper in his ear, "First time giving a speech on stage, how does it feel?"

"It feels hot." Li Luo tugged at the scarf around his neck. "Giving a speech under the national flag really gets your blood boiling."

"Not a single honest word." Ying Chanxi rolled her eyes at him.

"What I mean is," Li Luo pointed at the scarf around his neck, "your scarf is very warm. I get hot when I'm nervous, and it's making me sweat."

In reality, he wasn't nervous.

Although he had no such experience in his previous life, his mental age was, after all, that of a man in his thirties. He had also been on stage several times since his rebirth and was now someone who had seen the world.

A mere speech was nothing special.

Especially with the memory palace at his disposal, Li Luo delivered the speech entirely from memory, which earned him an appreciative nod from the Dean of Students who was hosting the flag-raising ceremony.

This time on stage was mainly because Attached No. 1 High School had arranged another monthly exam in December.

Li Luo had secured 15th place in the entire school, still the only student from a parallel class to make it into the top 40.

Thus, at the request of the Dean of Students, Li Luo from Class 8 of the first year was asked to prepare and share his learning methods and experiences at the flag-raising ceremony.

This was truly a first in two lifetimes.

In Li Luo's memory, the students who could go on stage to speak during the flag-raising ceremony were all incredibly impressive people.

For example, this person next to him named Ying Chanxi, who always held the first-place rank in the grade, was often called up to speak.

After the flag-raising ceremony ended, Li Luo followed Class 8's contingent back to the classroom.

Once the morning classes were over, after a simple lunch, Li Luo and Shi Yanran went to the classroom where the student council held its meetings and sat down.

As the president, Xu Youyu went over some routine matters before starting to discuss the New Year's Day Gala at the end of the month with everyone.

"The New Year's Day Gala will be held on December 31st. The next day, January 1st, is New Year's Day. Along with January 2nd and the two weekend days, that will be the New Year's holiday."

"On the day of the New Year's Gala, there will be a total of three stages of activities."

"The first stage is the class stamp-collecting activity in the morning. It will be organized by each class, with the entire grade as the activity area."

"Each class will set up a mini-game in their own classroom. Completing the game earns you a stamp."

"The second stage is the club experience activity in the afternoon, organized by the various interest-based clubs, taking place throughout the whole school."

"Each club will offer a simple club experience program. After completing a relatively basic experience, you can get a club stamp."

"The third stage is the bonfire party in the evening. The entire school will participate, and it will be held at the outdoor basketball court."

"Classes, clubs, and teachers are free to sign up for performance slots for stage performances and interactions."

"The specific procedures and rules have been distributed to you."

Xu Youyu scanned the room, then said, "The New Year's Day Gala is next Wednesday."

"So by this Wednesday noon, each class must report its mini-game activity. And by next Monday, you must prepare all the necessary props for the activity and arrange the personnel who will stay in the classroom."

"As for the clubs, it's the same after they've been notified. Finalize the experience program by Wednesday, and finalize personnel arrangements by next Monday."

"Additionally, for the bonfire party's performance slots, you can sign up voluntarily before this Wednesday noon. There are a total of 15 slots planned."

"In the past, they've always been fully booked, so I won't bother with any mandatory measures."

"That is all."

"Raise your hand if you have any questions."

After the regular meeting, Li Luo returned to his class and handed the arduous task of planning the class mini-game to the class's arts representative, Ren Zheng, asking her to decide on the mini-game by Tuesday evening.

So, before the evening self-study session began, Ren Zheng walked up to the podium and clapped her hands to signal for everyone's attention.

"Next Wednesday is the New Year's Day Gala. Each of our classes needs to prepare a mini-game in our classroom for students from other classes to participate in."

The petite Ren Zheng stood at the podium, speaking in a soft and gentle voice.

"So, in a moment, I'll have to trouble everyone to write a mini-game you find interesting on a slip of paper, one that can be carried out in the classroom, and then give it to me."

After she finished speaking, the bell for the evening self-study session rang.

Li Luo turned his head to look at Yan Zhusheng and saw that she had already taken out a pen and paper and was starting to think and write with great concentration. He couldn't help but lean over curiously to take a look.

But Yan Zhusheng immediately covered her paper and said with a serious little face, "No copying me."

"I won't copy, I'll just take a look," Li Luo said shamelessly. "Besides, if you want your mini-game to be chosen, don't you need more people to write down the same one?"

"Hmm..." Yan Zhusheng hesitated for a moment, then moved her hand away, letting Li Luo have a look.

Instrument Guessing Game: Prepare a dozen or so musical instruments. Have someone close their eyes, then have others play a piece of music. The person then has to guess which instruments were used in the piece.

Li Luo felt a bit embarrassed after reading it. "...Isn't this asking a bit too much? It's way beyond the curriculum."

Yan Zhusheng tilted her head, confused, "Is it? I think it's very simple."

"If you like it, you can give it a try. If it doesn't get picked, then there's nothing to be done."

"Oh." Yan Zhusheng nodded, then looked at Li Luo's paper. "So what are you writing?"

"Not showing you." Li Luo covered his paper, secretly writing on it with an air of mystery.

After he finished writing, Li Luo turned to look at Yan Zhusheng and noticed her gaze.

"I showed you, but you won't show me," Yan Zhusheng said with a serious little face. "I'm good, you're bad."

Li Luo: "...You're so childish. The adult world is full of deceit and trickery like this. I'm just letting you get used to it in advance."

"But we're not adults yet," Yan Zhusheng retorted matter-of-factly. "Let me see."

"Fine." Li Luo moved his hand, letting Yan Zhusheng take a look.

Instrument Guessing Game: ...

"You copied me." Yan Zhusheng narrowed her eyes.

"How can you call it copying when it's a matter among scholars?"

Li Luo reached over, took Yan Zhusheng's slip of paper, stacked it with his own, got up, and walked to Ren Zheng on the other side of the classroom to submit the slips.

After class, Ren Zheng had already collected a pile of paper slips.

Some students were brimming with ideas and wrote more than one, so when Ren Zheng came to Li Luo's desk with the slips, there was a stack of seventy or eighty of them.

"Class President, it's hard for me to decide alone. Should we look at them together?" Ren Zheng suggested. "It'll be faster this way."

Hearing this, Li Luo simply called over Xiuxiu and Shi Yanran as well, planning to find a classroom upstairs to discuss it.

Yan Zhusheng followed them upstairs out of curiosity, so Zhu Yufei, who loved to join in on the fun, quickly tagged along, clamoring to contribute to the grand undertaking.

And so, the six class committee members went to an empty classroom on the sixth floor, formed a circle, and began looking through the slips of paper.

"Blind Men and an Elephant."

"Picking up marbles with chopsticks."

"Folding paper airplanes."

"Table tennis."

"These all feel so old-fashioned."

"Are there any newer ideas?"

"How about this one? I think it's very original." Zhu Yufei shamelessly handed over a slip of paper.

Xiuxiu took it out of curiosity, but her face immediately turned red as she threw the paper on the table. "What is this! Who wrote it? Are they looking for a beating!"

Li Luo found it strange, so he leaned over for a look, then immediately became serious. "This one's no good, vetoed."

Yan Zhusheng next to them picked up the slip of paper and read it out loud, word for word, "Maid Guessing Game. Have several girls wear identical maid outfits, with the same hairstyle and hair accessories."

"A participating student chooses one of the maids, who walks up and does a twirl in front of them. After the student has observed carefully, the maid returns to the group."

"The student is blindfolded. The maids switch places and stand with their backs to the student. The student then removes the blindfold and guesses which maid they had just observed."

Shi Yanran: "...Tang Bohu choosing his bride, Qiuxiang?"

Ren Zheng: "...What a weird taste."

"Is this one no good?" Zhu Yufei asked in a small voice.

"You're not the one who wrote it, are you?" Xiuxiu looked at him sideways.

"How could that be!" Zhu Yufei righteously denied it. "I would never write something like this. This looks like something Zhang Guohuang would write."

"There's another identical one here." Yan Zhusheng pulled out a slip from the pile, which also said "Maid Guessing Game."

Li Luo glanced at it, nodded, and chuckled. "Mm, he's not lying. That last one was written by Zhang Guohuang. This one is his."

"Class President!" Zhu Yufei shouted. "How can you tarnish my good name out of thin air?"

"I recognize both of your handwriting," Li Luo said, looking as if Zhu Yufei had never seen the world. "I can recognize everyone's handwriting in the class."

"For example, this one was written by Xiuxiu, right?"

"This one is Sister Yanran's."

"This one is Ren Zheng's."

The others confirmed, then looked at each other in bewilderment.

Although everyone was already well aware of Li Luo's memory, they didn't expect him to have a skill like this up his sleeve.

"Actually, this Maid Guessing Game isn't entirely out of the question," Xiuxiu suddenly broke into a brilliant smile. "We could just change the staff. Just have Zhu Yufei and Zhang Guohuang pick a few boys to wear the maid outfits, right?"

"Ahem." Zhu Yufei quickly snatched the two slips of paper, tore them to shreds, and stuffed them into his pants pocket. "I think we should look at the others."

Ren Zheng rolled her eyes at him and continued looking through the other slips.

A short while later, Shi Yanran's eyes suddenly lit up, and she held up two slips of paper for everyone to see. "I think this one is quite creative."

"Instrument Guessing Game?" Xiuxiu and Ren Zheng leaned closer. "Guessing instruments? Won't that be a little difficult?"

Li Luo pretended to lean in next to them and then said, "The difficulty can be adjusted. If three instruments are too hard, then use two. If that's still too hard, just use one. If they still can't guess, then there's no excuse."

"Mm, the difficulty can indeed be adjusted. We can just test it out in class beforehand," Shi Yanran nodded. "But where are we going to find so many instruments? We'd need to prepare at least three or four types, right? And some instruments are not easy to bring into a classroom, like a piano."

"I have a lot at home," Yan Zhusheng raised her hand and said. "Flute, violin, xiao, guitar, pipa, hulusi, melodica, and this."

As she spoke, Yan Zhusheng took out the harmonica Li Luo had given her from her pocket and gave it a little shake.

Hearing her say this, Xiuxiu immediately nodded in agreement. "I think it sounds pretty good, but if we want to play several instruments at once, we'll need at least a few people who can play them, right?"

"I can play all of these a little," Yan Zhusheng said, then pointed at Li Luo. "He can play the guitar."

"I think Chen Zhongqi can play the pipa."

"I learned the flute when I was little, so playing a simple tune shouldn't be a problem," Ren Zheng said, raising her hand.

"Then finding two or three more people who can play other instruments shouldn't be too hard," Shi Yanran said. "How about we keep this game as a candidate?"

After a round of discussion, more than half the class period had passed.

Although they found a few other interesting mini-games later, most were eliminated due to inconvenient venue, props, or personnel arrangements.

With the active intervention of Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng, Class 8's mini-game activity was temporarily decided to be the "Instrument Guessing Game."

On the way back from the sixth-floor classroom to the third floor, Zhu Yufei let out a long sigh. "Sigh, my Maid Guessing Game is gone."

"Serves you right," Xiuxiu rolled her eyes at him.

"By the way," Zhu Yufei suddenly remembered something and turned to look at Li Luo, asking curiously, "who wrote this Instrument Guessing Game? Class President, can't you tell from the handwriting? Let me see which lucky dog wrote it."

Li Luo chuckled twice. "Take a guess."

Nearby, Yan Zhusheng skipped along with a light and cheerful pace, humming a little tune all the way back to the classroom.

(End of this chapter)
